Exercise A

Two Ways to Run a Country

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

Although the United Kingdom and the United States share a language and a long history, their systems of government are very different.

The United Kingdom is a constitutional monarchy. This means that the country has a king or queen as head of state, but real political power is held by Parliament. Laws are made by Parliament, which is divided into two houses: the House of Commons, whose members are elected by the people, and the House of Lords. The leader of the government is the Prime Minister, who is normally the leader of the largest party in the House of Commons. The UK does not have a single written constitution; instead, its rules have been developed over many centuries.

The United States, in contrast, is a federal republic with a written constitution that was signed in 1787. The head of state is the President, who is elected by the people every four years and is both head of state and head of government. Power is divided between the federal government in Washington and the fifty individual states. Laws are made by Congress, which, like the British Parliament, has two parts: the House of Representatives and the Senate. A system of "checks and balances" is used so that no single person or group can become too powerful.

Exercise B

The Passive Voice

In formal texts about politics, the passive is very common because the action matters more than who does it. Choose the correct passive form for each gap.

Fill in the Gaps

1 In the UK, laws by Parliament.

2 The US Constitution in 1787.

3 After an election, the Prime Minister by the King to form a government.

4 Members of the House of Commons by the people.

5 Last year, a new law to protect the environment.

6 The American President every four years.

7 Many important decisions in Washington.

8 The White House in the late 18th century.

Exercise C

Active → Passive

Read each active sentence, then choose the correct passive version. Keep the same tense!

Choose the Passive Version

1 The people elect the President.
→ The President by the people.

2 Parliament makes the laws.
→ The laws by Parliament.

3 Congress passed the law in 2020.
→ The law by Congress in 2020.

4 They will hold an election next year.
→ An election next year.

5 The government has increased taxes.
→ Taxes by the government.

6 Workers built the Capitol in 1800.
→ The Capitol in 1800.

7 The King opens Parliament every year.
→ Parliament by the King every year.

8 People speak English in both countries.
→ English in both countries.
